title: Growing a path graph
description: A path is built one edge at a time; each proof step adds an edge established by the current goal.
source:
inductive Reach : Nat → Nat → Prop where
  | edge12 : Reach 1 2
  | edge23 : Reach 2 3
  | edge34 : Reach 3 4
  | edge45 : Reach 4 5
  | edge56 : Reach 5 6
  | trans {a b c : Nat} : Reach a b → Reach b c → Reach a c

theorem path_1_to_6 : Reach 1 6 := by
  apply Reach.trans
  · exact Reach.edge12
  · apply Reach.trans
    · exact Reach.edge23
    · apply Reach.trans
      · exact Reach.edge34
      · apply Reach.trans
        · exact Reach.edge45
        · exact Reach.edge56

steps.explanation: The initial goal is to prove that there is a path from node 1 to node 6.
Reach.trans splits the path goal into two reachability goals with an intermediate node, while Lean also displays a type-inference goal.
The edge from node 1 to node 2 is established, so the first reachability goal is solved.
The remaining path is split again, asking for a path from node 2 to an intermediate node and then from that node to node 6.
The edge from node 2 to node 3 is established, solving the current first reachability goal.
The remaining path is split again, introducing another intermediate node before reaching node 6.
The edge from node 3 to node 4 is established, solving the current first reachability goal.
The remaining path is split again, extending the chain toward node 6.
The edge from node 4 to node 5 is established, solving the current first reachability goal.
The final edge from node 5 to node 6 completes the path from node 1 to node 6.
